We have over 400,000 cases confirmed in the United States at over 14,000 deaths. At the same time, we are facing an economic catastrophe. That crisis is the direct result of the government policies that have been put in place to limit the spread of the pandemic. As a consequence of those government policies, over 10 million Americans have lost their jobs just in the last couple of weeks. Millions of small businesses are facing enormous economic pressures as government policies have blocked them from their customers and effectively shut them down from restaurants to bars to movie theaters to hair salons and nail salons small businesses across the country and in texas are hurting mightily two weeks ago congress passed $2 trillion in emergency relief legislation. I don't refer to that bill as stimulus because its focus was different. Its focus was on providing short-term bridge loans to help people make it through this crisis and get to the other side. The only way we'll get our economy back, the only way we'll bring those jobs back is to reopen the economy is to get people back to work is to remove the government prohibitions on employees going to the office and on customers going to small business and so we have an urgency both at the federal level and at the state and local level to address both those crisis to address the public health crisis listening to the science and the doctors and the medical professionals to stop the spread of this deadly disease but at the same time to get the economy moving as quickly as humanly possible, because the economic catastrophe will have a very real cost in human lives as well.
